title: PHY 101 ( UNINIGER ) : PHYSICAL QUANTITIES, UNIT AND DIMENSIONS
subject: PHY 101

questions.question: A physical quantity is defined as which of the following?
questions.explanation: A physical quantity is any measurable property of a physical system.

questions.question: Physical quantities are broadly classified into which two categories?
questions.explanation: Physical quantities are classified into fundamental and derived quantities.

questions.question: Fundamental quantities are independent and cannot be derived from any other quantity.
questions.explanation: Fundamental quantities form the foundation and cannot be derived from others.

questions.question: The number of universally recognized fundamental quantities is which of the following?
questions.explanation: There are seven universally recognized fundamental quantities.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a fundamental quantity?
questions.explanation: Mass is one of the seven fundamental quantities.

questions.question: Units are defined as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Units are agreed-upon standards for measurement.

questions.question: Adding a length to a velocity is considered nonsensical because they describe different physical phenomena.
questions.explanation: Different physical quantities have different units and cannot be directly added.

questions.question: Units serve to distinguish between different quantities and provide which of the following?
questions.explanation: Units provide a common reference for measurement.

questions.question: The modern internationally recognized system for fundamental units is known by which abbreviation?
questions.explanation: The Metre-Kilogram-Second system is known as the MKS system.

questions.question: Fundamental units cannot be obtained by combining other units.
questions.explanation: Fundamental units are independent and form the basis for other units.

questions.question: In the MKS system, length is measured in which unit?
questions.explanation: The MKS system measures length in metres.

questions.question: In the MKS system, mass is measured in which unit?
questions.explanation: The MKS system measures mass in kilograms.

questions.question: Derived units are obtained by combining fundamental units through which mathematical operations?
questions.explanation: Derived units are formed by multiplying or dividing fundamental units.

questions.question: The derived unit for area is expressed as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Area is length times length, so its unit is square metres.

questions.question: The derived unit for velocity is expressed as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Velocity is distance divided by time, so its unit is metres per second.

questions.question: The derived unit for force is expressed as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Force is mass times acceleration, so its unit is kilogram metre per second squared.

questions.question: Volume is a derived quantity and its unit is expressed as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Volume is length cubed, so its unit is cubic metres.

questions.question: The International System of Units is derived from which French term?
questions.explanation: SI is derived from the French term Systeme International d'Unites.

questions.question: Which two supplementary units are recognized in the SI system?
questions.explanation: The SI system recognizes plane angle and solid angle as supplementary units.

questions.question: The supplementary unit for plane angle is measured in which unit?
questions.explanation: Plane angle is measured in radians.

questions.question: The supplementary unit for solid angle is measured in which unit?
questions.explanation: Solid angle is measured in steradians.

questions.question: One foot is equivalent to how many metres?
questions.explanation: One foot is exactly 0.3048 metres.

questions.question: One inch is equivalent to how many centimetres?
questions.explanation: One inch is equal to 2.54 centimetres.

questions.question: One hour is equivalent to how many seconds?
questions.explanation: One hour contains 60 minutes, each with 60 seconds, totaling 3600 seconds.

questions.question: One day is equivalent to how many seconds?
questions.explanation: One day consists of 24 hours, each with 3600 seconds, totaling 86400 seconds.

questions.question: One year is approximately equivalent to how many seconds?
questions.explanation: One year is approximately 3.154 x 10^7 seconds.

questions.question: One litre is equivalent to how many cubic metres?
questions.explanation: One litre is equal to 10^-3 cubic metres.

questions.question: 180 degrees is equivalent to how many radians?
questions.explanation: A straight angle of 180 degrees is equal to π radians.

questions.question: One radian is approximately equivalent to how many degrees?
questions.explanation: One radian is approximately 57.3 degrees.

questions.question: One degree is equivalent to how many radians?
questions.explanation: One degree is equal to 1.745 x 10^-2 radians.

questions.question: One Angstrom is equivalent to how many metres?
questions.explanation: One Angstrom is defined as 10^-10 metres.

questions.question: One kilometre is equivalent to how many metres?
questions.explanation: The prefix kilo means one thousand, so 1 km = 10^3 m.

questions.question: Dimensions express how a physical quantity relates to which fundamental quantities?
questions.explanation: Dimensions express relationships in terms of length, mass, and time.

questions.question: Dimensions are represented using which notation?
questions.explanation: Dimensions are conventionally represented using square brackets.

questions.question: An equation is dimensionally correct if both sides have which property?
questions.explanation: For an equation to be dimensionally correct, both sides must have identical dimensions.

questions.question: Dimensional analysis alone cannot guarantee an equation's full correctness because it ignores which elements?
questions.explanation: Dimensional analysis cannot account for dimensionless constants or vector directions.

questions.question: Trigonometric, exponential, and logarithmic functions are considered to be which of the following?
questions.explanation: Trigonometric, exponential, and logarithmic functions and their arguments are dimensionless.

questions.question: The dimension of force is given by which expression?
questions.explanation: Force is mass times acceleration, so its dimension is [MLT-2].

questions.question: The dimension of acceleration is given by which expression?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is velocity divided by time, giving the dimension [LT-2].

questions.question: The dimension of power is given by which expression?
questions.explanation: Power is energy divided by time, which has the dimension [ML2T-3].

questions.question: The dimension of density is given by which expression?
questions.explanation: Density is mass divided by volume, giving the dimension [ML-3].

questions.question: The dimension of momentum is given by which expression?
questions.explanation: Momentum is mass times velocity, which has the dimension [MLT-1].

questions.question: The dimension of area is given by which expression?
questions.explanation: Area is length squared, so its dimension is [L2].

questions.question: The dimension of volume is given by which expression?
questions.explanation: Volume is length cubed, so its dimension is [L3].

questions.question: Electric current has which dimension?
questions.explanation: Electric current is a fundamental quantity with the dimension [A].

questions.question: Luminous intensity has which dimension?
questions.explanation: Luminous intensity is a fundamental quantity with the dimension [J].

questions.question: Verifying the equation v2 = u2 + 2as using dimensional analysis shows it is which of the following?
questions.explanation: All terms in the equation v2 = u2 + 2as have the same dimension [L2T-2].

questions.question: Verifying the equation v2 = u + at2 using dimensional analysis shows it is which of the following?
questions.explanation: The left-hand side has dimensions [L2T-2] while the right-hand side terms have [LT-1] and [L].

questions.question: The period T of a simple pendulum depends on length L, mass M, and gravity g. Dimensional analysis gives T proportional to which expression?
questions.explanation: Dimensional analysis yields T = k square root of L/g.

questions.question: The velocity V of a wave on a string depends on tension T, mass m, and length l. The dimensional equation is V = kTa m^b l^c. Solving for the exponents gives which result?
options: a equals one, b equals one, c equals one
a equals negative half, b equals half, c equals half
a equals one, b equals negative one, c equals zero
questions.explanation: Dimensional analysis yields the exponents a=1/2, b=-1/2, and c=-1/2.
